Q: Question about the 'non-linear' behaviour of the Python interpreter in Jupyter A:

Jupyter doesn't look ahead, and the error is likely happening at exactly the same spot. The reason you don't see the "Pdf read." message is most likely because the kernel crashes before it has time to send the latest chunk of the output stream to you.

Q: Get all indexes on string columns Postgres A:

Your query misses expression indexes, domains over text types, and doesn't exclude collations unaffected by glibc (ICU, C/POSIX).
On PostgreSQL 14+, skip the manual query entirely. PG tracks collation versions for you:

REINDEX DATABASE yourdb;
ALTER DATABASE yourdb REFRESH COLLATION VERSION;

PG will warn you about exactly which collations have a version mismatch after the glibc upgrade.

**
For a more correct manual query (PG 13 or earlier, or pre-upgrade audit):**

SELECT
    n.nspname        AS schema,
    c.relname        AS table,
    i.relname        AS index,
    pg_get_indexdef(ix.indexrelid) AS index_definition
FROM pg_index ix
JOIN pg_class i ON i.oid = ix.indexrelid
JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = ix.indrelid
JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace
WHERE n.nspname NOT IN ('pg_catalog', 'information_schema')
  AND ix.indisvalid
  AND (
    -- Expression indexes (conservatively flagged)
    ix.indexprs IS NOT NULL
    OR
    -- Simple columns with collation-sensitive types
    EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM unnest(ix.indkey) k(attnum)
      JOIN pg_attribute a ON a.attrelid = c.oid AND a.attnum = k.attnum
      WHERE k.attnum > 0
        AND pg_catalog.format_type(a.atttypid, a.atttypmod) ~*
            '(text|character varying|character\(|varchar|bpchar|citext|name)'
    )
  )
  -- Exclude indexes using only ICU or C/POSIX collations (unaffected by glibc)
  AND NOT (
    SELECT bool_and(co.collname IN ('C', 'POSIX') OR co.collprovider = 'i')
    FROM unnest(ix.indcollation) coll_oid
    JOIN pg_collation co ON co.oid = coll_oid
    WHERE coll_oid <> 0
  )
ORDER BY n.nspname, c.relname, i.relname;

This update improves your original by catching expression indexes, detecting domains in text via pattern matching instead of a fixed OID list, skipping ICU and C/POSIX collations since they’re locale-independent, and checking the actual collation the index uses.
